Name: difficulty_contraction_failure
Title: Difficulty That Won't Shrink: Overthinking as a Failure of the Internal Difficulty Signal to Contract as Reasoning Progresses
Short Hypothesis: LLMs carry a linearly-decodable, attention-head-mediated 'difficulty' representation that prior work reads only once, before generation. We hypothesize this signal should contract during a chain of thought as sub-goals are resolved, and that overthinking occurs when this contraction fails - the internal difficulty stays high even after residual work reaches zero. Concretely: reading the SAME final-layer difficulty heads and difficulty direction at step boundaries, decoded difficulty should decline monotonically with truncate-and-resume residual work on well-behaved traces, and overthought traces are those where it plateaus high despite zero residual work; steering those heads toward the easy pole once residual work is low should induce early, correct termination, and this effect must remain after matching on a confidence/uncertainty probe.
Related Work: A recent cluster of interpretability work establishes that LLMs linearly encode problem difficulty in pre-generation activations, localize it to specific final-layer attention heads (Probing the Difficulty Perception Mechanism, 2025; A Shared Geometry of Difficulty, 2026; LLMs Encode Their Failures, 2026), and use it to allocate compute at the input level (ACTSC 2026, FR-Ponder 2025, AdaCtrl 2025, CODA 2026, UAB 2026). All treat difficulty as a static, pre-generation property of the input and set a budget or sample count before or independent of the trace; none examine how the difficulty representation evolves DURING generation or connect overthinking to a failure of that representation to update. Our contribution is orthogonal and temporally specific: (1) the same difficulty direction/heads can be read at intermediate CoT positions and normally contract as work is completed; (2) overthinking is a specific dynamical failure - non-contracting difficulty despite resolved residual work; (3) we intervene on the difficulty heads mid-generation to induce contraction. Critically, we separate this from confidence/uncertainty dynamics: confidence early-exit acts on a correctness/uncertainty readout, whereas we act on the difficulty heads and require the causal effect to survive matching on a confidence probe, so the claim is about difficulty specifically, not a generic confidence correlate.
Abstract: Deployed reasoning models waste large amounts of compute by continuing to reason after a problem is effectively solved, inflating tokens, latency, and serving cost with unreliable stopping. Recent interpretability work shows that LLMs linearly encode problem difficulty via specific attention heads and that this signal, read before generation, can allocate compute. But difficulty is not static: as a model resolves sub-goals, the residual problem becomes easier and its internal difficulty should shrink. We hypothesize that overthinking is a failure of this contraction - the internal difficulty stays elevated even after residual work reaches zero, driving continued reasoning. We replicate a linear difficulty probe and localize difficulty-sensitive final-layer heads on DeepSeek-R1 distills (1.5B-14B) and Qwen3, then read the signal at each step of a chain of thought on GSM8K, MATH500, AIME, and GPQA. We test whether difficulty normally contracts as residual work (truncate-and-resume) decreases, whether overthought traces show stalled difficulty, and whether the contraction-failure metric predicts wasted tokens better than absolute difficulty, length, or a confidence probe. We causally validate the difficulty heads by steering them toward the easy pole mid-generation once residual work is low - including a negative control that steers them when residual work is NOT low - and require the effect to persist after matching a confidence probe, isolating difficulty from confidence. We compare token savings, wall-clock latency, and per-query cost at equal accuracy against input-level difficulty budgeting, length steering, and confidence early-exit, and analyze failures where genuine difficulty persists. The work reframes a static difficulty representation as a dynamical control signal for interpretability, decoding, and agentic-inference practitioners.
Experiments:
Compute fits an academic node (<= 8xA100-80GB). Primary model: DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-7B, frozen; only linear probes are trainable, and interventions are activation edits (no weight updates). Scale sweep: R1-Qwen distills 1.5B/7B/14B and Qwen3-8B. Decoding: temperature 0.6, top-p 0.95, max 16k thinking tokens, seeds 0/1/2 on every reported number. CoT segmented into steps by newline/step delimiters. Datasets, used as released: GSM8K test (1319), MATH500 (500), AIME 2024+2025 (60), GPQA-Diamond (198); difficulty labels from Easy2Hard-AMC-style annotations plus empirical per-item pass-rates (32 samples/item). All thresholds (contraction cutoff, residual-work threshold, k) are FIXED on a training split before any evaluation, to avoid post-hoc success criteria. Residual work is defined precisely as: truncate the trace at step t, force termination, read the forced answer; residual work at t = the minimum number of additional true steps (from the full trace) after which forced-exit accuracy first reaches and holds the final accuracy - reported alongside a simpler proxy (forced-exit correctness at t) for robustness.

Experiment 1 (H1 - Difficulty is decodable and head-mediated, including mid-trace): Replicate a linear difficulty probe and localize difficulty-sensitive final-layer heads, then test readability at intermediate positions. Train on pre-generation activations (40% of items), evaluate on 60% held out. Identify difficulty heads by ablation impact on probe output; report which layer/head set. Decisive metric: held-out probe AUROC/R^2 pre-generation and at intermediate positions. Convincing: pre-generation AUROC >= 0.75 (replication) and intermediate AUROC >= 0.70, with a small head set (<= 10) whose ablation drops probe AUROC by >= 0.1. Indecision: intermediate AUROC in [0.6, 0.7]. Negative (< 0.6): difficulty is encoded only pre-generation - this is the MINIMUM FALSIFIER: the paper then becomes a strong negative result (difficulty is not trackable during reasoning) and the novelty shifts to that finding.

Experiment 2 (H2 - Difficulty normally contracts): Form the step-wise difficulty trajectory over boundaries. Decisive metric: mean signed change in decoded difficulty from first to last step across correctly solved traces. Convincing: contracts on average (paired p < 0.01, mean drop > 0.3 in normalized probe units) on the majority of correctly solved traces. Indecision: mean drop in [0.1, 0.3]. Negative (< 0.1 or increasing): difficulty does not contract, refuting H2.

Experiment 3 (H3 - Contraction failure tracks residual work and predicts waste): Contraction failure = area between difficulty and residual-work trajectories after residual work hits zero (steps subsampled every 2nd boundary). First test difficulty-vs-residual-work correlation, then whether contraction failure predicts wasted tokens. Decisive metric: out-of-sample 5-fold R^2 of contraction failure predicting wasted tokens, minus best competitor among absolute pre-generation difficulty, trace length, and a confidence probe. Convincing: correlation r > 0.4 and contraction failure beats the best competitor by >= 0.10 R^2 on at least three datasets. Indecision: r in [0.2, 0.4] or R^2 advantage in [0.02, 0.10]. Negative (r < 0.2 or advantage <= 0.02): overthinking is not this pattern.

Experiment 4 (H4 - Difficulty heads causally gate continuation, isolated from confidence): At low-residual-work / high-difficulty boundaries, steer the localized difficulty heads toward the easy pole (or add the negative difficulty direction) and measure the effect on termination-token probability and continuation length, vs. (i) control heads, (ii) norm-matched random directions, and (iii) confidence-probe steering matched in magnitude. Ablations over head choice, layer choice, and intervention timing establish specificity. Decisive metric: increase in termination probability under difficulty-head steering minus that under control-head AND under confidence-probe steering. Convincing: difficulty-head steering raises termination probability by >= 15 points and shortens continuation by >= 20%, significantly above control/random AND above confidence-probe steering, with accuracy on already-solved items within 2 points. Indecision: gain in [5, 15] points over control. Negative (< 5 points over control, or indistinguishable from confidence-probe steering): difficulty heads are not a distinct causal gate.

Experiment 5 (H4 - Negative control on timing regime): Apply the same difficulty-head steering when residual work is NOT low (early, genuinely-hard boundaries) and confirm it does NOT induce correct early termination there. Decisive metric: termination-probability increase under steering in the low-residual-work regime minus that in the high-residual-work regime. Convincing: the termination effect is concentrated in the low-residual-work regime (difference >= 10 points), and steering in the high-residual-work regime harms accuracy (confirming it should not fire). Indecision: a weak regime difference. Negative (effect equal across regimes): early termination is not specific to the intended regime, weakening the mechanism.

Experiment 6 (H4 - Training-free intervention: savings, latency, cost): Online, read step-wise difficulty; when difficulty fails to contract but a residual-work probe (trained on Experiment-3 labels, 40/60 split) predicts low residual work for k consecutive steps, steer difficulty heads toward easy. k and threshold fixed on the training split. Report the full accuracy-vs-token Pareto curve. Systems compared on all four datasets: intervention vs. (a) no intervention, (b) fixed truncation matched to intervention budget, (c) input-level difficulty budgeting (CODA/AdaCtrl-style), (d) length steering, (e) confidence-based early-exit. Decisive metric: token reduction at equal accuracy. Secondary: mean tokens, accuracy, wall-clock latency, per-query serving cost. Convincing: >= 25% token reduction within 1 point on GSM8K and MATH500, on or above every baseline frontier. Indecision: reduction in [10%, 25%] or a frontier-tie - the dynamical characterization (Experiments 1-5) is then the standalone contribution. Negative (< 10% or > 1 point loss): no usable savings.

Experiment 7 (H4 - Underthinking guard): On the hardest quartile where residual work truly stays large, verify the trigger does not fire and does not induce premature termination. Decisive metric: hard-item accuracy drop vs. residual-work threshold. Convincing: < 1 point at the deployed threshold. Indecision: 1-3 point drop. Negative (> 3 point drop): the gate cannot protect hard items, bounding H4.

Experiment 8 (H1/H3 - Generality across data and scale): Transfer probe, head set, and trigger across datasets and the 1.5B/7B/14B/Qwen3-8B models without retraining. Decisive metric: transferred-probe AUROC relative to in-domain and intervention token-savings retention. Convincing: transfer retains >= 80% of in-domain AUROC on at least three scales; savings hold within 10 relative percent. Indecision: retention in [60%, 80%]. Negative (< 60%): the difficulty-dynamics signal is idiosyncratic across models.
Risk Factors and Limitations: The difficulty direction may entangle with confidence/uncertainty, blurring the distinction from confidence early-exit; we control by comparing difficulty-head steering against magnitude-matched confidence-probe steering and require the difficulty heads to be causally distinct. Difficulty may not be cleanly readable at intermediate positions (the probe was trained pre-generation); if it is only encoded pre-generation the dynamical framing collapses into a strong negative result (the stated minimum falsifier). The truncate-and-resume residual-work measure is noisy and compute-heavy; we subsample steps and report a simpler proxy. Steering difficulty heads could disrupt genuine hard-problem reasoning (underthinking); the residual-work-gated trigger, negative-control regime test, and threshold analysis address this. Intervention gains may not exceed strong difficulty-budgeting baselines; the standalone contribution is then the dynamical, causal characterization, useful to interpretability, decoding/efficiency, and agentic-inference communities that need reliable in-flight stopping. Results may be model-family and scale specific.
